script.base: This is a small-favorite dome game, not a shootout and not a slog. The book has PHI leading a close one: PHI 23.0, MIN 20.5, spread only 2.5, total 43.5. PHI's weeks 4-6 offense is a split attack, not a one-man show: Barkley 37 carries for 131 yards (3.54 YPC, about 12 carries a game) with Hurts adding 17 carries for 79, while the targets are Brown 26, Goedert 24 and Smith 17. MIN's weeks 3-5 offense (different window than PHI, reason not in the pack) is Mason 45 carries for 225 (5.0 YPC, about 15 a game) and Jefferson 29 targets for 324 yards and 347 air yards, with Wentz the QB who shows up in the rush log (7 carries, 29 yards). Base flow: competitive through the fourth quarter, both QBs throw, Mason keeps a real carry share because MIN is not a 3.5-point-or-worse dog, and PHI's late lead is a field goal not a blowout, so starter snaps should hold.
script.flip1: PHI scores early and leads by two scores at halftime. The favorite then runs the clock: Barkley's carries rise, Hurts' scramble yards and the Brown/Smith/Goedert yardage stall, and MIN has to abandon Mason's 15-carry role. Jefferson, Addison and Hockenson targets spike in a trail script. That flip helps a Jefferson over and hurts a Goedert over and any Barkley rush under.
script.flip2: Mason at 5.0 YPC controls the clock against a PHI run defense allowing 4.75 YPC, and it gets easier if Jalen Carter (heel, questionable) sits. The total drifts under 43.5. Wentz faces PHI's 32% blitz, where MIN is -0.36 EPA per dropback versus +0.07 with no blitz, so Jefferson's 12.0 aDOT shots die. PHI also never needs a full pass volume, so Goedert's 8-target role shrinks. Both overs lose together in this grind.

injury_fallout: Pre-game nflverse injury report, not the 90-minute inactives (those are not in the pack). Out: MIN LB Andrew Van Ginkel (neck) and PHI TE Grant Calcaterra (oblique). Van Ginkel out, with fellow LB Blake Cashman questionable (hamstring), is the coverage fallout on MIN's defense. Backup linebacker names are not in the pack. Missing linebackers normally help the TE and the receiving back: Goedert already has 24 targets for 166 yards in three games, Barkley has 10 targets for 98 yards. Calcaterra was only 4 targets and 34 yards in that same window, so Goedert already is the TE; the out tag is a small target bump, not a new role. MIN QB J.J. McCarthy is questionable (ankle). The weeks 3-5 rush log lists C. Wentz 7/29 and does not list McCarthy, so this read assumes Wentz is the quarterback who produced Jefferson's 324 yards and is void if McCarthy is active and changes the shot profile. MIN T Brian O'Neill (knee) and C Michael Jurgens (hamstring) are questionable; if either tackle or center sits, pressure on Wentz rises and Jefferson's deep yards are the casualty, while Hockenson and Mason checkdowns would gain. PHI G Landon Dickerson is questionable (ankle); if he sits, Barkley's already poor 3.54 YPC gets worse and PHI may throw shorter, which is a small tailwind for Goedert and a headwind for a Barkley rush over. PHI DT Jalen Carter is questionable (heel); if he sits, Mason's 5.0 YPC run game faces a softer interior. MIN DEs Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (hip) and Tyler Batty (knee) are questionable depth rushers, not charted, and are not treated as a pass-rush collapse. No PHI corner or safety is listed out, so Jefferson is not stepping into a named backup coverage player.

matchup.shell: No man/zone rate and no MOFO/MOFC charting in the pack, so shell is not called. What the pack does show: MIN blitzes 46% and the location split is extreme. Middle 10.33 YPA on 30 attempts, left 5.2 YPA on 55, right 5.37 YPA on 52. MIN has allowed only 8 passes of 20+ (pack figure 8/150) in 5 games. That is a middle-of-field problem, not an outside-corner problem. PHI's shell, also uncharted for man/zone, has the opposite map: right 7.15 YPA on 89 attempts, left 6.3 on 74, middle a tighter 5.42 on 36, plus 15 passes of 20+ (pack figure 15/208) in 6 games.
matchup.pressure: MIN blitz rate 46%. PHI EPA per dropback is -0.02 versus the blitz and +0.03 with no blitz, so PHI is roughly neutral, not a blitz-beater. Pressure that gets home should cut Brown's 311 air yards on 26 targets (12.0 aDOT, only 130 yards, 5.0 yards per target) and push quick throws to Goedert and Barkley. PHI blitz rate 32%. MIN EPA per dropback is -0.36 versus the blitz and +0.07 with no blitz. That is the loudest QB split in the pack and it is aimed at Wentz, the quarterback in the recent rush log. If PHI brings pressure, Jefferson's 347 air yards are the part of the MIN offense that dies, and Hockenson (75 air yards on 17 targets, 4.4 aDOT) and Mason's screens (7 targets, -29 air yards) are the checkdown winners.
matchup.bleeds: MIN bleeds the middle and is without Van Ginkel, with Cashman also questionable. MIN does not bleed the outside and does not bleed explosives (8 of 20+ in 5 games versus PHI's 15 in 6). MIN rush defense allows 4.61 YPC and 21 runs of 10+ in 5 games, so it is not a wall, but Barkley has been at 3.54 YPC with Hurts taking 17 carries. PHI bleeds explosives and the right side (7.15 YPA on 89 attempts) and is ordinary against the run at 4.75 YPC with 22 runs of 10+ in 6 games. PHI's middle (5.42 YPA) is the spot they do not bleed, which is why Hockenson is not the overlap.
matchup.overlap: The core overlap on the PHI side is Goedert, not Brown. Goedert has 24 targets and 224 air yards over three games, essentially co-primary with Brown's 26 targets, and he is the tight end working the middle where MIN allows 10.33 YPA. Brown's 311 air yards attack the outside and the deep ball, which is the part of MIN that has held (5.2 and 5.37 YPA, only 8 explosives). Smith (17 targets, 192 yards, 167 air yards, 11.3 yards per target) is efficient but his alignment is not charted, so he is not forced into the middle overlap. On the MIN side the overlap is Jefferson: 29 targets, 324 yards, 347 air yards, 12.0 aDOT, into a PHI defense that has allowed more 20+ passes and 7.15 YPA to the right. Addison's 14 targets and 155 yards are a 2-game sample against an 77.5 line and are not the primary. Nailor is 13 targets for 66 yards into the same defense and has not earned the overlap.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and both overs lost. Goedert lost because the 110 was one play, the real tight-end line in this offense has been 19, 33 and 37, and PHI led late so Hurts handed it to Barkley even though Barkley is at 3.54 YPC. The missing linebacker did not matter because MIN played the shell that has held the outside and also took the middle away for one week, or because Dickerson sat and the whole PHI dropback game stalled. Jefferson lost because PHI blitzed into the -0.36 EPA split, O'Neill or Jurgens sat, McCarthy played on the ankle instead of the Wentz sample that produced 324 yards, and the 75-yard floor showed up again. 81.5 was simply the 5-game median, and a 20.5 implied team total never required a 108-yard receiver. That counter is strongest on Goedert's yardage history and on Jefferson's blitz number. It is not stronger than the middle-bleed plus Van Ginkel-out plus 8-target stack, which is why Goedert stays flagged instead of cut. It is strong enough that Jefferson is only a lean. Both lose together if flip 2 hits and Mason controls the clock.
slip_story: One story only: a competitive dome game with both passing games live, PHI 23.0 and MIN 20.5, spread 2.5, no blowout bench risk, total 43.5 not used as a blanket over or under. Goedert recyds over is the MIN-middle and 46% blitz leg. Jefferson recyds over is the PHI-explosive and right-side leg. They can both hit in a one-score game and they do not need opposite scripts. Do not add Brown, because his air yards attack the part of MIN that has held. Do not add a Barkley rush under, because the base script has the favorite running late. Do not add Addison, Mason, Hockenson, Nailor, Dillon or Scott; none has a clean overlap plus a form trend that survives the base script. No touchdown legs. No second market on Goedert or Jefferson. No price is saved, so this is a candidate slip for the checklist, not a bet, and the stake proposal on both is 0.
